function: Channel prediction: predicts next-step downlink CSI from past uplink CSI of a massive MIMO base station (TDD and FDD) with a GPT-2-based predictor (pp. 3–4).
system: MISO-OFDM: BS dual-polarized UPA (Nh = Nv = 4), single-antenna users; 2.4 GHz uplink, 8.64 MHz bandwidth, TDD and FDD; no RIS (p. 8).
method: GPT-2 (first six layers) fine-tuned with LoRA, cross-modal attention alignment and semantic prompts; supervised NMSE plus alignment loss; lightweight student by attention-relation distillation; Adam (pp. 4–8).
data_channel: QuaDRiGa-generated 3GPP UMa channels: 9000 training, 1000 validation, 1000 test samples, speeds 10–100 km/h; own dataset, no link (p. 8).
test_conditions: Train UMa, 10–100 km/h; test held-out UMa; zero-shot UMi (p. 10) and FDD highway, 50–120 km/h (p. 11); 10% training data (p. 9); noisy-CSI SNR sweep (p. 9).
baselines: Non-learned: No-Prediction (uplink CSI reused as downlink); learned: CNN, RNN, LSTM, GRU, Transformer, and the LLM-based LLM4CP (p. 8, Figs. 7–14).
metrics: NMSE (dB) versus speed and SNR, average NMSE (Table I), parameter count and inference time (Table II) (pp. 8–12).
complexity: Table II (p. 12): CSI-ALM 11.8M trainable, 93.8M total parameters, 198.2 ms inference; CSI-ALM-Light 0.349M parameters, 2.41 ms; single RTX A6000 (p. 13).
q1_support: p. 8: "we utilize the channel generator QuaDRiGa [40] to generate a time-varying CSI dataset that complies with the 3GPP standard"; the same page: "We consider the 3GPP Urban Macro (UMa) channel model", used for training, validation, and test.
q2_support: p. 10: "The zero-shot generalization performance for the TDD systems in UMi scenario". Models trained on UMa (p. 8) are applied directly to UMi (Figs. 13–14, p. 10) and to a highway FDD scenario (Fig. 15, p. 11).
q3_support: p. 8: "we directly used the CSI values of the uplink channel over the next L steps as the predicted CSI values for the downlink channel" is the non-learned No-Prediction curve; p. 8: "we employ CNN [23], RNN [24], GRU [26], LSTM [25], Transformer [27]" and "LLM4CP [37] as baseline methods" are the learned ones, all compared on NMSE (Figs. 7–14).
q4_support: p. 12: "Inference speed and complexity comparison" (Table II): CSI-ALM 93.8M parameters and 198.2ms, CSI-ALM-Light 0.349M parameters and 2.41ms.
q5_support: p. 8: "we utilize the channel generator QuaDRiGa [40] to generate a time-varying CSI dataset". The dataset is self-generated with a public simulator, and no link to code or data appears in the paper, including its conclusion (pp. 13–14).
notes: pdf_text.py misorders and drops the text of pp. 8–13 (figure legends come out as NUL characters, and the QuaDRiGa passage sits under the page 9 marker), so pp. 8–15 were read from page images; cited pages are the real PDF pages.
